questions.title: Who is the player?
questions.prompt: Is the Avatar a fixed character or one the player makes?
questions.context: Souls-likes usually let you build your own character. A fixed Avatar makes story scenes and past-life visions easier to write.

options.label: Fixed Avatar
options.detail: Their own name, face and backstory.

options.label: Custom Avatar
options.detail: The player picks name and looks, like Elden Ring.

options.label: Fixed backstory, custom look
options.detail: Story stays strong; players still make them their own.

questions.title: Why now?
questions.prompt: Why are the Spirit World and the physical world clashing in this era?
questions.context: Vaatu is sealed in the Tree of Time and Harmonic Convergence is thousands of years away, so something else has to thin the barrier.

options.label: Vaatu pushing from inside the Tree
options.detail: His darkness leaks out and weakens the barrier everywhere.

options.label: Humans broke a sacred pact
options.detail: A spirit site was desecrated and the spirits retaliated.

options.label: The last Avatar died with work unfinished
options.detail: Balance slipped in the gap before you awoke.

questions.title: Past lives
questions.prompt: How many past lives does the player meet in visions?
questions.context: Only Wan plus original ancient Avatars are lore-safe in our era.

options.label: Wan + 2 originals
options.detail: Tight and personal.

options.label: Wan + 4 originals
options.detail: One from each nation.

options.label: Wan + many brief echoes
options.detail: Lots of short visions, few deep characters.

questions.title: Opening scene
questions.prompt: Where do you wake up, and what's the first thing you see?
questions.context: This is the first minute of the game. It should show the world is wrong without explaining it. Your starting element can change where this happens.

questions.title: Finding masters

questions.title: One master or many?
questions.prompt: Can the player learn from more than one master per element?
questions.context: Each master teaches a different sub-style, so this decides how different two playthroughs can be.

options.label: One per element
options.detail: A permanent choice. Builds differ a lot; strong reason to replay.

options.label: One first, more later
options.detail: Choose one, and late in the game you can train with others.

options.label: Learn from all of them
options.detail: Go wherever you like; each master adds their sub-tree.

questions.prompt: Does your choice of master affect which ending you get?

options.label: Yes, through their questlines

options.label: No
options.detail: Masters only affect your build.

options.label: Only the secret ending

questions.title: How many endings?
questions.prompt: Roughly how many endings should the game have?
questions.context: Elden Ring has around 5–6. Every ending must leave Vaatu sealed.

options.detail: Easier to make each one feel big.
Like Elden Ring.

options.label: 2 plus a secret
options.detail: Two main paths and one hidden ending.

questions.title: Avatar State stages

options.label: 3 stages

options.detail: One per element learned.

options.label: 5 stages
options.detail: Four from elements, plus final mastery at the Tree of Time.

questions.title: Open-order difficulty
questions.prompt: How do we balance difficulty when players can go anywhere?

options.label: Enemies scale

options.label: Mix
